item.text: {"text":"Recent research supports separating observed behavior, explicit preference and evidence sufficiency. [ReCRec (2024)](https://zhoushengisnoob.github.io/papers/TOIS2024.pdf) highlights that noninteraction conflates lack of exposure with dislike; it cannot establish rejection. [LARA (SIGIR 2025)](https://www.nist.gov/publications/llm-assisted-relevance-assessments) warns that LLM relevance judgments can be biased and fail to transfer between datasets, supporting human-assisted assessment. [Attribute or Abstain (EMNLP 2024)](https://aclanthology.org/2024.emnlp-main.463/) provides a methodological precedent for evidence attribution and abstention. These support components of the proposed audit, but do not validate its exact four-way taxonomy or establish that topical relatedness means willingness to choose now.\n\nProposed application to the twenty training-user audits: label each recommendation “choose now” only with explicit current acceptance, “broadly related” with supported interest overlap, “explicit rejection” with actual negative feedback, or “insufficient evidence” when judgment requires assumptions. Attach source IDs, exact evidence spans and timestamps; separate user statements from annotator inference. Record compatibility, complementarity, duplication, quantity and mood only when supported; histories alone establish neither ownership nor unresolved demand. Keep unavailable attributes and simulator traits unknown. Pilot a written codebook with examples, independently double-annotate a category-balanced sample, measure agreement before adjudication, and retain disagreements. Report raw agreement plus nominal Krippendorff’s alpha, per-label counts, abstention rate, and assessable coverage by user/category; keep abstentions in denominators. These are proposed reporting choices, requiring local validation: [JUDGE-BENCH (2025)](https://clp.ling.uni-potsdam.de/publications/Bavaresco-2025.pdf) finds task-dependent LLM–human alignment and recommends task-specific human validation. Use the audit as supplementary diagnosis while retaining macro validation HR@10 for model selection."}
